subject: POC/trial planning: workload & success criteria follow-up
summary: Post-demo follow-up capturing success criteria, evaluation plan, expected traffic profile (RPS, token lengths, concurrency, burst patterns), timeline and ownership for a 4-week POC with Acme Health.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Acme POC workload intake

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the POC properly: 

Goals / success criteria (what success looks like):
- API latency under 200ms P50 for user-facing summarization flows (low-latency path)
- Average cost per 1k tokens below $0.60 for inference (target to compare against current spend)
- No functional regressions on 3 core prompt families (clinical note summarization; medication extraction; patient triage classification)
- Integration hooks (SAML + audit logs) validated by security team during the trial window

Workload intake (what you told us on call) — can you confirm/adjust:
- Expected steady-state RPS: 3–5 rps (peak 20 rps)
- Typical request token lengths: 80–400 tokens (median ~150)
- Concurrency: 4 concurrent client sessions during business hours; spikes up to 30 concurrent connections during morning batch processing windows
- Burst pattern: daily morning burst (08:00–09:30 PT) and weekly batch on Mondays 02:00–03:00 PT (~10x steady-state)

Proposed POC plan (4 weeks):
1) Week 0: workload intake + signed MSA/POC SOW
2) Week 1: integration + sample dataset ingestion + baseline perf run
3) Week 2: tuning (batching/quantization suggestions) + security review
4) Week 3: final eval vs success criteria + handoff checklist

Action items for you:
- Please confirm the workload numbers above (RPS, token ranges, concurrency, burst windows) — Tom or Alice
- Share a redacted sample of the three prompt families (or a synthetic set) — Alice
- Provide the security point of contact for SOC 2 evidence and SAML setup — Alice

Action items for us:
- I will share the evaluation plan spreadsheet and an initial workload-profile template (attached).
- Marissa will coordinate the security checklist and schedule a short review with our infosec engineer.

Attachments: poc-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation matrix + timeline), workload-profile.csv (template)

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick 15-min call if you want to walk these items together.
\Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112
\---

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Acme POC workload intake

Thanks Ben — this is great, and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications / confirmations from our side: 

- RPS: confirmed steady-state 4 rps, peak sustained up to 18 rps (so your 20 rps peak is fine).
- Tokens: median ~140, 95th percentile ~430 (we have occasional long notes) — we can provide a small sample export (redacted) by EOD Wed.
- Concurrency: our realtime UI will maintain ~6 concurrent sessions; batch job Monday mornings may spike to ~35 concurrent streams for a short window.
- Burst pattern: agree on morning window; Monday batch ~02:30 PT, typically lasts ~20–30 minutes.

Success criteria: we are mostly aligned. Can we add a reliability target of 99.5% availability during business hours for the POC? Also would like to include token-level cost estimates in your eval plan.

Security contact: Tom Rivera (tom.rivera@acmehealth.com) — he will be your point for SOC 2 Qs and SAML setup.

We will attach the redacted samples and a short list of example prompts tomorrow. Looking forward to the plan.
\Best,
Alice
Director, Clinical AI
Acme Health
\On Mon, Apr 26, 2027 at 4:04 PM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the POC properly: ...

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: POC evaluation plan + questions on reliability target

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks for the quick confirmation. Attached is the evaluation spreadsheet (poc-eval-plan.xlsx) and the workload profile template we discussed (workload-profile.csv). Key notes and a couple of quick questions below: 

1) Reliability SLA for POC: we can target 99.5% availability during business hours for the test window. For the POC we provide a POC SLA and runbooks; if we hit degradations we will trigger automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant to preserve availability. Does Acme want the fallback enabled (yes/no)?

2) Token cost estimates: we've added a cost tab with per-1k-token estimates for the models we tested. We'll run the sample dataset once Week 1 to produce expected spend projections.

3) Workload details: to tune batching and concurrency, we need a small CSV with these columns: timestamp,event_type,request_tokens,response_tokens,client_id. The attached template has an example row. If you can provide ~48 hours of representative traffic (redacted) that will give us a good baseline for queueing and batching behavior.

4) Timing: proposed kickoff next Monday (May 3). That gives us Week 0 activities this week for SOW and simplest SAML exchange. Is that OK?

Action items (updated):
- Acme: confirm fallback behavior; share 48h traffic export + sample prompts + SOC 2 contact (Tom) — Alice/Tom
- Redwood: schedule kickoff for May 3, run baseline once sample data is in, provide initial cost projection by end of Week 1 — Ben/Marissa

If you prefer, we can do a 15-min call tomorrow to walk through the fallback option and the template columns.
\Thanks,
Ben
\

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC evaluation plan + questions on reliability target

Hi Alice / Tom — great to see alignment. One quick note from ops/security:

- We will enable the automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model during the POC to preserve availability unless you explicitly tell us not to. Fallback will be logged and flagged for review; it requires no configuration on your side.
- For the SOC 2 evidence collection, Tom, our questionnaire and the initial artifact list are in the Drive link Ben shared. I'll set up a 30-min intro with our infosec engineer (Sara) next week — please send 2 available windows.

Confirming kickoff: May 3 is fine from our side. Ben / I will be present for the first integration sync.
